about: Shared parity fixture for the magic-shelf count compiler (MagicShelfCountCompiler) and the UI BookRuleEvaluatorService.

"books" is exactly the list-view stream a viewer who sees both libraries receives: Jackson NON_NULL, so a null value is an absent key (never write an explicit null: the UI reads Number(null) as 0 but Number(undefined) as NaN).
Each book carries a "fixture" object that is not part of the DTO: it holds what the backend needs to rebuild the entities. The UI spec strips it before evaluating.

fixture.files are the book_file rows in id order (ids only fix the order). primaryFile, alternativeFormats and supplementaryFiles are derived from them with library formatPriority the way BookMapperV2.getPrimaryBookFile does.

fixture.progress is the viewer's user_book_progress row (null = none; readStatus null and "UNSET" both serialize as "UNSET"); fixture.otherUserProgress is another user's row that must not affect the viewer.
fixture.isPhysical / fixture.isComic null exist only on H2 (the production columns are NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE).
"deletedBooks" are inserted with deleted = TRUE; the stream never shows them and no case expects them.
Tag, category and mood names that differ only by case or trailing space are distinct rows (exact-name lookup).
Book ids, file ids and library ids are fixture ids: map them to the generated ids, and insert files in the listed order.
metadata.authors [] (book 12), tags [] (book 12) and categories [] (book 13) are explicit on purpose: the list-view DTO strips empty collections, and the evaluator reads [] and an absent list alike.
cases.json entries: {name, production?, filterJson (exactly as stored), now (UTC), expect: [ids ascending] | "UNSUPPORTED" | "INVALID", required?, reason?, collationSensitive?}.
The production cases are named prod-<magic shelf id>: their filterJson is the stored string of that production shelf, verbatim, and every one is required.

required: true means the server must answer OK with exactly these ids; false means it may answer UNSUPPORTED instead, but any count it gives must be these ids. reason is the expected UNSUPPORTED reason (informational).

collationSensitive: an accent-insensitive or PAD SPACE collation (MariaDB) can give other ids; H2 compares exactly and must match. Every array expect was computed by the real BookRuleEvaluatorService, and does not depend on the time zone.
